correctness.rationale: Reconstructed both languages and all reachable continuation classes in RESULT.md lines 33–65. For a nonpower, 2^k−c for k≥s has binary expansion α at k=s and 1^(k−s)β for k>s; prefixing zeros gives 0*( {α} ∪ 1+β ). It is essential that β starts with zero and |α|<s. Beyond a nonzero prefix, before its first zero the r exceptional suffixes augment 1*β by distinct words shorter than s; a longer initial run reaches 1*β alone. After consuming the first zero, exactly h overlap-prefix lengths leave two suffixes; the longer suffix distinguishes the h pairs. Singletons are precisely the s proper suffixes of β, including the empty suffix, since exceptional-only suffixes also occur among them. The start residual alone has accepted words with arbitrarily many initial zeros, and an impossible prefix reaches the empty residual. For c=2^(s−1), the language 0*({ε} ∪ 1+0^(s−1)) gives the start, sink, 1*0^(s−1), and s−1 singletons, including the s=1 case with no singletons. The bounds follow from 1≤r+h≤|α|≤s−1 and the two stated choices of c realize the endpoints, including their coincidence at s=2. Inspected the bundled checker and saved finite output; the source script was not executed, and the proof is independent of the finite test range.
